          "citation": "docs/adr/0021-review-swarms-until-clean.md::Consumed-ladder amendment — the next step after the last stage, 2026-11-20",
          "end_line": 301,
          "excerpt": "## Consumed-ladder amendment — the next step after the last stage, 2026-11-20\n\nThe maintainer decided on 2026-11-20, in the conversation of that day's run,\nthat a consumed ladder no longer stops the lane for a question. Decision 7\nsaid that exhausting the eligible stages with accepted findings stops and\nreports to the maintainer. In the night runs of 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20\nthat stop held two lanes (slip-counter, findings-per-model) until the\norchestrator applied the maintainer's answer by hand; a run's history cannot\nbe reset, so a new loop run was never an option.\n\nDecision 7 now reads, for this case: when every eligible stage of a run is\nconsumed, at least one review round completed in that run, and the last\nround was not clean, the loop ends without a further round and names the\nnext step. While a taken row of that round is open, the next step is the\nrepair of those rows; once every taken row is fixed, the next step is the\nphase-6 review, which checks that last repair through its full `make verify`\nand the reviewer's read of the whole diff. This holds also when the loop's\ndiff was cut at the line bound, because phase 6 reads the complete diff in\nthe worktree (`decisions.md` Q-5). When zero review rounds completed in the\nrun (total stage outage), the loop still stops and reports to the maintainer\ninstead of skipping phase 4b (`decisions.md` Q-4). No final-model repeat\nfollows, as before.\n\nUnchanged: the repair brake of decision 7 (two consecutive rounds each with\naccepted findings all caused by repairs, Origin `fix-r`, stop and go to the\nmaintainer) and every other stop of this ADR. The amendment changes where a\nconsumed ladder leads, not when the loop stops.\n\nThe runner carries the rule (house rule 9): `review-loop` ends such a run\nwith exit 0 and one line on standard output, `next: repair <change>` or\n`next: review <change>`, and does not start either verb itself (bead\ncoding-harness-hwll, change `ladder-next-step`, its `decisions.md` Q-2).\nUntil that change merges, the orchestrator applies this amendment by hand,\nas `AGENTS.md` states.\n",

          "truncated": false
        }

          "citation": "AGENTS.md::House rules",
          "end_line": 93,
          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "end_line": 388,
          "excerpt": "def _stage2_row(tokens: list[str], pid: str, elapsed: str, changes: frozenset[str]) -> ProcessRow | None:\n    script = next((i for i, token in enumerate(tokens) if _is_stage2_script(token)), None)\n    if script is None or script + 1 >= len(tokens) or tokens[script + 1] not in KNOWN_VERBS:\n        return None\n    if script != 0:\n        if not re.fullmatch(r\"python(?:\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)*)?\", Path(tokens[0]).name):\n            return None  # the executable owns the invocation, not a preceding argument\n        if any(not token.startswith(\"-\") or token in {\"-c\", \"-m\", \"--\"} for token in tokens[1:script]):\n            return None\n    verb = tokens[script + 1]\n    change = NOT_READ\n    arguments = iter(tokens[script + 2 :])\n    value_options = {\n        \"--model\",\n        \"--class\",\n        \"--availability-reported\",\n        \"--seats\",\n        \"--handover\",\n        \"--stage-failed\",\n        \"--reason\",\n        \"--root\",\n    }\n    for token in arguments:\n        if token == \"--stage2-off\":\n            # Its reason is optional. A known change or another option must\n            # remain available to the positional/option reader below.\n            following = next(arguments, None)\n            if following is None:\n                break\n            if following not in changes and not following.startswith(\"-\"):\n                continue  # the explicit reason\n            token = following\n        if token in value_options:\n            next(arguments, None)\n            continue\n        if token.startswith(\"-\"):\n            continue  # options may stand between the verb and the change\n        if token in changes:\n            change = token\n        break  # only the first non-option token can name the change\n    return ProcessRow(pid=pid, elapsed=elapsed, label=verb, change=change)\n",

          "excerpt": "def parse_processes(ps_text: str, changes: frozenset[str]) -> list[ProcessRow]:\n    \"\"\"The runner invocations and verification processes of one `ps` table.\n\n    Token matching only: a string inside an unrelated command - a shell\n    wrapper, an editor, an echo - is discarded, never reported.\n    \"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    for line in ps_text.splitlines():\n        parts = line.split(None, 2)\n        if len(parts) < 3 or not parts[0].isdigit() or not ETIME.fullmatch(parts[1]):\n            continue  # the header line and anything unshaped\n        pid, elapsed, command = parts\n        tokens = command.split()\n        if not tokens:\n            continue\n        row = _stage2_row(tokens, pid, elapsed, changes) or _verify_row(tokens, pid, elapsed)\n        if row is not None:\n            rows.append(row)\n    return rows\n",

          "citation": "docs/adr/0021-review-swarms-until-clean.md::Consumed-ladder amendment — the next step after the last stage, 2026-11-20",
          "end_line": 301,
          "excerpt": "## Consumed-ladder amendment — the next step after the last stage, 2026-11-20\n\nThe maintainer decided on 2026-11-20, in the conversation of that day's run,\nthat a consumed ladder no longer stops the lane for a question. Decision 7\nsaid that exhausting the eligible stages with accepted findings stops and\nreports to the maintainer. In the night runs of 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20\nthat stop held two lanes (slip-counter, findings-per-model) until the\norchestrator applied the maintainer's answer by hand; a run's history cannot\nbe reset, so a new loop run was never an option.\n\nDecision 7 now reads, for this case: when every eligible stage of a run is\nconsumed, at least one review round completed in that run, and the last\nround was not clean, the loop ends without a further round and names the\nnext step. While a taken row of that round is open, the next step is the\nrepair of those rows; once every taken row is fixed, the next step is the\nphase-6 review, which checks that last repair through its full `make verify`\nand the reviewer's read of the whole diff. This holds also when the loop's\ndiff was cut at the line bound, because phase 6 reads the complete diff in\nthe worktree (`decisions.md` Q-5). When zero review rounds completed in the\nrun (total stage outage), the loop still stops and reports to the maintainer\ninstead of skipping phase 4b (`decisions.md` Q-4). No final-model repeat\nfollows, as before.\n\nUnchanged: the repair brake of decision 7 (two consecutive rounds each with\naccepted findings all caused by repairs, Origin `fix-r`, stop and go to the\nmaintainer) and every other stop of this ADR. The amendment changes where a\nconsumed ladder leads, not when the loop stops.\n\nThe runner carries the rule (house rule 9): `review-loop` ends such a run\nwith exit 0 and one line on standard output, `next: repair <change>` or\n`next: review <change>`, and does not start either verb itself (bead\ncoding-harness-hwll, change `ladder-next-step`, its `decisions.md` Q-2).\nUntil that change merges, the orchestrator applies this amendment by hand,\nas `AGENTS.md` states.\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "reference": "Consumed-ladder amendment — the next step after the last stage, 2026-11-20",
          "start_line": 268,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },

          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::review_loop",
          "end_line": 13267,
          "excerpt": "def review_loop(root: Path, change: str, availability_reported: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"One round of phase 4b, until a round is clean (ADR 0021).\n\n    A fresh run discovers its free members through a forced live refresh and\n    pins the stage snapshot; every later call takes the run's next unconsumed\n    stage. The stops come before any stage: undecided or evidence-incomplete\n    rows first, then a clean previous round, then the repair brake (two\n    consecutive rounds whose accepted findings all begin `fix-r`), then spent\n    stages - each naming the round or the maintainer, and none reset by a\n    release or an edited configuration (ADR 0021, decision 9). One call\n    completes one round; a swarm's members run concurrently and merge into one\n    heading and one id series; an attempt whose every member failed completes\n    no round and consumes no stage.\n    \"\"\"\n    record = read_record(change, root)\n    if record is not None:\n        refusal = undecided_refusal(record_rows(record), \"decide them first\")\n        if refusal:\n            raise Refused(refusal)\n    findings_text = \"\"\n    findings_path = folder_of(root, change) / \"findings.md\"\n    if findings_path.exists():\n        findings_text = findings_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    refusal = origin_refusal(record, findings_text)\n    if refusal:\n        raise Refused(refusal)\n    if record is not None:\n        refusal = released_overlap_refusal(record, findings_text)\n        if refusal:\n            raise Refused(refusal)\n    if record is None:\n        refusal = lost_record_refusal(change, root, findings_text)\n        if refusal:\n            raise Refused(refusal)\n    # The snapshot before the stops: a released block without the runner's snapshot is refused here,\n    # never read as a finished run (DL-A-2 of the deep review).\n    state = None if restarted_fresh(record, findings_text) else read_state(record, findings_text)",

          "citation": "scripts/harness.py::main",
          "end_line": 524,
          "excerpt": "def main(argv: list[str] | None = None, *, ask: Ask = input, out: Out = print, today: date | None = None) -> int:\n    args = parser().parse_args(argv)\n    root: Path = args.root.resolve()\n    try:\n        if args.verb == \"time-log\":\n            return time_log(root, args, out=out, today=today or date.today())\n        given: dict[str, Any] = {name: getattr(args, name) for name in RECORDING}\n        if any(v is not None for v in given.values()):\n            flags = {name: \"--\" + name.replace(\"_\", \"-\") for name in RECORDING}\n            absent = [flags[n] for n, v in given.items() if v is None or not str(v).strip()]\n            if absent:\n                raise Refused(\n                    f\"recording an answer needs all four of {', '.join(flags.values())}; missing or blank: {', '.join(absent)}\"\n                )\n        role = answering_role(root)\n        message = message_path(root)\n        day = today or date.today()\n        if given[\"change\"] is not None:\n            return record_adr(\n                root,\n                given[\"change\"],\n                given[\"answer\"],\n                given[\"reason\"],\n                given[\"stated_in\"],\n                out=out,\n                today=day,\n                role=role,\n                message_path=message,\n            )\n        if not sys.stdin.isatty():\n            raise Refused(\n                \"run this yourself in a terminal — the questions are for the maintainer to answer; \"\n                \"an answer stated elsewhere is recorded with --change, --answer, --reason and --stated-in\"\n            )\n        return decide_adr(root, ask=ask, out=out, today=day",

          "end_line": 1506,
          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept; one retry after the configured pause, then the declared\n  fallback through Pi; at most three rounds (\"The spec review before the plan\n  card\").\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`. On every route it first refuses, before any model\n  starts, a refused class or a `bounded`, `feature` or `architectural` change\n  without a current spec review free of open `[AMBIGUITY]` rows.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021).           "excerpt": "### Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests\n\nEvery change says in its spec header what kind of change it is — `class:`,\none of four:\n\n- `spike` — answers a question; its output is a recommendation.\n- `bounded` — changes an existing, readable flow without deciding anything new.\n- `feature` — a self-contained deliverable that changes what the system must\n  do or how it is checked.\n- `architectural` — a new subsystem or a break of an interface; it carries its\n  ADR already, so it is not asked.\n\n**The design phase 2b goes by class** (decision D-14,\n`prompts/02b-design.md`): an `architectural` change always runs it; a `feature`\nruns it or says in one sentence of its `spec.md` why not; a `bounded` change\nand a `spike` never run it. after a research swarm every obligation item answered and linked (`research_items`, `research_neighbours`; minimums are no ceiling) | [`01a-interview.md`](../prompts/01a-interview.md) |\n| 2 | Spec | `plans/changes/<name>/spec.md` | validator green, no open `[DECISION]`; after a research swarm `neighbours:` and every criterion's `*Basis:*` match the research (`research-handoff`) | [`02-spec.md`](../prompts/02-spec.md) |\n| 2a | Spec review *(not for a spike)* | rows for `findings.md`, dimension `SPEC`; then the revised `spec.md` | a current review of the spec before the plan card, the final draft after round three excepted; every row worked into the spec or rejected with a reason; no open `[AMBIGUITY]`; at most three spec-review rounds, a fourth only by the maintainer's recorded answer (§4, \"The spec review before the plan card\") | [`02a-spec-review.md`](../prompts/02a-spec-review.md) |\n| 2b | Design *(by class)* | `plans/changes/<name>/design.md` | validator green; for an `architectural` change, an ADR draft in it | [`02b-design.md`](../prompts/02b-design.md) |\n| 3 | Plan | `plans/changes/<name>/plan.md` | validator green | [`03-plan.md`](../prompts/03-plan.md) |\n| 4 | Implement | code + tests | `make verify` green | [`04-implement.md`](../prompts/04-implement.md) |\n| 4b | Review loop *(stage 2)* | the loop rows — outside the repository until the phase-6 verdict, then in `findings.md` (`release-loop`) | rounds until a clean round — the free swarm, the Flash swarm, then the paid ladder (ADR 0021); The gate `interview-minimums`\n(`scripts/check_interview_minimums.py`) counts the records at the spec gate\nand in `make verify`: only distinct, maintainer-answered records count, an\nagent's answer, an open question and a repeated confirmation count for\nnothing, and the check sees ADR paths in every diff state — committed,\nstaged, unstaged, untracked.           "end_line": 301,
          "excerpt": "## Consumed-ladder amendment — the next step after the last stage, 2026-11-20\n\nThe maintainer decided on 2026-11-20, in the conversation of that day's run,\nthat a consumed ladder no longer stops the lane for a question. Decision 7\nsaid that exhausting the eligible stages with accepted findings stops and\nreports to the maintainer. In the night runs of 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20\nthat stop held two lanes (slip-counter, findings-per-model) until the\norchestrator applied the maintainer's answer by hand; a run's history cannot\nbe reset, so a new loop run was never an option.\n\nDecision 7 now reads, for this case: when every eligible stage of a run is\nconsumed, at least one review round completed in that run, and the last\nround was not clean, the loop ends without a further round and names the\nnext step. While a taken row of that round is open, the next step is the\nrepair of those rows; once every taken row is fixed, the next step is the\nphase-6 review, which checks that last repair through its full `make verify`\nand the reviewer's read of the whole diff. This holds also when the loop's\ndiff was cut at the line bound, because phase 6 reads the complete diff in\nthe worktree (`decisions.md` Q-5). When zero review rounds completed in the\nrun (total stage outage), the loop still stops and reports to the maintainer\ninstead of skipping phase 4b (`decisions.md` Q-4). No final-model repeat\nfollows, as before.\n\nUnchanged: the repair brake of decision 7 (two consecutive rounds each with\naccepted findings all caused by repairs, Origin `fix-r`, stop and go to the\nmaintainer) and every other stop of this ADR. The amendment changes where a\nconsumed ladder leads, not when the loop stops.\n\nThe runner carries the rule (house rule 9): `review-loop` ends such a run\nwith exit 0 and one line on standard output, `next: repair <change>` or\n`next: review <change>`, and does not start either verb itself (bead\ncoding-harness-hwll, change `ladder-next-step`, its `decisions.md` Q-2).\nUntil that change merges, the orchestrator applies this amendment by hand,\nas `AGENTS.md` states.\n",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line sh",

          "excerpt": "### Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests\n\nEvery change says in its spec header what kind of change it is — `class:`,\none of four:\n\n- `spike` — answers a question; its output is a recommendation.\n- `bounded` — changes an existing, readable flow without deciding anything new.\n- `feature` — a self-contained deliverable that changes what the system must\n  do or how it is checked.\n- `architectural` — a new subsystem or a break of an interface; it carries its\n  ADR already, so it is not asked.\n\n**The design phase 2b goes by class** (decision D-14,\n`prompts/02b-design.md`): an `architectural` change always runs it; a `feature`\nruns it or says in one sentence of its `spec.md` why not; a `bounded` change\nand a `spike` never run it. Nothing checks this until the change-artefact\nvalidator lands (bead coding-harness-jc3); the review before the merge holds\nit.\n\n**The interview goes by class too** (maintainer, 2026-10-08): a `feature`\nowes at least three distinct, substantive questions; creating or changing an\nADR (one it claims under `adr_files`) raises the debt to five in whatever class the change carries; a `spike`\nowes its three topics or a reasoned skip; a `bounded` change one answered\nquestion or a reasoned skip. What the gate counts and what the review judges\nstands in §2, the paragraph after the phase table.\n\n**Only a `feature` owes an answer to the ADR question:** is this change an\narchitecture decision that needs an ADR? The spec author proposes, in the same\nheader: `change: <folder name>` and `adr_question: {proposed: \"yes\"|\"no\",\nreason: \"<one sentence>\"}` (`prompts/02-spec.md`). The proposal only proposes.\nThe maintainer answers, and the answer lives in\n`decisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml`, in the format of the LakeSwitch pilot\n(`schema_version: 1`), so LakeSwitch reads it unchanged.\n\nThere are two ways to answer, both through `python3 scripts/harness.py decide\nadr`:\n\n1. **Typed in a terminal** by the maintainer: the command shows each open\n   question with its title, anchor and proposal, takes `y` or `n` and a\n   one-sentence reason, and asks for three explain-back lines at the end.\n2. **Stated in the conversation**, and recorded by the agent exactly as stated,\n   one change per run: `--change <name> --answer yes|no --reason \"<English\n   sentence>\" --stated-in \"<where the maintainer said it>\"`. The source goes\n   into the commit message, not into the answer file.\n\nEither way the command writes the answer files and a commit message, and\nstages, commits and merges nothing. The gate `adr-answers`\n(`scripts/check_adr_answers.py`, in `decisions/gates.yaml`) holds every\nfeature, active or archived, to an answer file that exists, has the format and\nnames its own change.\n\n**A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request**, or\nasks an agent in the conversation to merge it. There is no commit signing in\nCoding Harness (ADR 0008, 2026-09-30). A pull request that adds, changes or\nremoves a file `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` — an ADR, an ADR\nanswer, the rule set — is a **decision pull request**: its title is\n`decide(<scope>): <the decision as a statement>`, it carries the label\n`decision`, and its body begins with the block from\n`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md` — what is decided, that the merge\nis the confirmation, what it confirms, the options and what follows. Every\nother pull request takes `.github/pull_request_template.md`, whose first lines\nsay that nothing is decided. How an agent merges on request is in\n`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The merge\".\n\nWhat this does not do:\n\n- The gate holds existence and format only. It cannot see who wrote an answer\n  or who merged it.\n- Agents act under the maintainer's GitHub account, so nobody can tell from\n  GitHub who pressed merge. The merge rule is a rule, not proof.\n- The ask rules in `.claude/settings.json` are a brake against an accidental\n  merge, not a lock. Since the night-stall-guard change (2026-11-09) they match\n  precise",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "end_line": 301,
          "excerpt": "## Consumed-ladder amendment — the next step after the last stage, 2026-11-20\n\nThe maintainer decided on 2026-11-20, in the conversation of that day's run,\nthat a consumed ladder no longer stops the lane for a question. Decision 7\nsaid that exhausting the eligible stages with accepted findings stops and\nreports to the maintainer. In the night runs of 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20\nthat stop held two lanes (slip-counter, findings-per-model) until the\norchestrator applied the maintainer's answer by hand; a run's history cannot\nbe reset, so a new loop run was never an option.\n\nDecision 7 now reads, for this case: when every eligible stage of a run is\nconsumed, at least one review round completed in that run, and the last\nround was not clean, the loop ends without a further round and names the\nnext step. While a taken row of that round is open, the next step is the\nrepair of those rows; once every taken row is fixed, the next step is the\nphase-6 review, which checks that last repair through its full `make verify`\nand the reviewer's read of the whole diff. This holds also when the loop's\ndiff was cut at the line bound, because phase 6 reads the complete diff in\nthe worktree (`decisions.md` Q-5). When zero review rounds completed in the\nrun (total stage outage), the loop still stops and reports to the maintainer\ninstead of skipping phase 4b (`decisions.md` Q-4). No final-model repeat\nfollows, as before.\n\nUnchanged: the repair brake of decision 7 (two consecutive rounds each with\naccepted findings all caused by repairs, Origin `fix-r`, stop and go to the\nmaintainer) and every other stop of this ADR. The amendment changes where a\nconsumed ladder leads, not when the loop stops.\n\nThe runner carries the rule (house rule 9): `review-loop` ends such a run\nwith exit 0 and one line on standard output, `next: repair <change>` or\n`next: review <change>`, and does not start either verb itself (bead\ncoding-harness-hwll, change `ladder-next-step`, its `decisions.md` Q-2).\nUntil that change merges, the orchestrator applies this amendment by hand,\nas `AGENTS.md` states.\n",

        }

The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept; one retry after the configured pause, then the declared\n  fallback through Pi; at most three rounds (\"The spec review before the plan\n  card\").\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`. On every route it first refuses, before any model\n  starts, a refused class or a `bounded`, `feature` or `architectural` change\n  without a current spec review free of open `[AMBIGUITY]` rows.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry.           "excerpt": "def _run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:\n    \"\"\"The verb `main` parsed, with the runner's refusals mapped to their exit codes.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        if args.spec_review_inventory:\n            if args.verb or args.change:\n                raise Refused(\"--spec-review-inventory takes no verb and no change; it measures every change itself.\")\n            if (\n                any(\n                    value is not None\n                    for value in (\n                        args.stage2_off,\n                        args.klass,\n                        args.seats,\n                        args.availability_reported,\n                        args.model,\n                        args.handover,\n                        args.stage_failed,\n                        args.reason,\n                        args.row_status,\n                        args.reason_text,\n                    )\n                )\n                or args.restart\n            ):\n                raise Refused(\"--spec-review-inventory takes no other option.\")\n            refuse_repository_git(Path(args.root))\n            return spec_review_inventory(Path(args.root))\n        if not args.verb:\n            raise Refused(\"name a verb, or run --spec-review-inventory for the morning inventory.\")\n        # Validate verbs here, after the verb-less inventory option has been handled.\n        known = sorted([*VERBS, \"session\", \"prepare-explore\"])\n        if args.verb not in known:\n            raise Refused(\n                f\"`{args.verb}` is no verb of this runner; choose from {', '.join(known)}, \"\n                \"or run --spec-review-inventory without one.\"\n            )\n        if (\n            args.stage2_off is not None\n            and not args.change\n            and (Path(args.root) / \"plans\" / \"changes\" / args.stage2_off).is_dir()\n        ):\n            raise Refused(\n                f\"the change name `{args.stage2_off}` was taken as the --stage2-off reason; \"\n                \"put the change before the flag or write --stage2-off=REASON.\"\n            )\n        if args.stage2_off is not None and args.verb not in {\"explore\", \"implement\", \"repair\"}:\n            raise Refused(\"--stage2-off applies only to explore, implement and repair.\")\n        if args.klass is not None and args.verb not in {\"explore\", \"prepare-explore\"}:\n            raise Refused(\"--class belongs to the explore and prepare-explore verbs alone.\")\n        if args.seats is not None and args.verb != \"prepare-explore\":\n            raise Refused(\"--seats belongs to prepare-explore alone.\")\n        if args.availability_reported is not None and args.verb not in {\"explore\", \"review-loop\"}:\n            raise Refused(\"--availability-reported belongs to the explore and review-loop verbs alone.\")\n        refuse_repository_git(Path(args.root))\n        if (args.stage_failed is not None or args.reason is not None or args.restart) and args.verb != \"release-loop\":\n            raise Refused(\"--stage-failed, --restart and --reason belong to release-loop alone.\")\n        if args.supersedes is not None and args.verb != \"release-loop\":\n            raise Refused(\"--supersedes belongs to release-loop --restart alone.\")\n        if args.verb != \"triage\" and (args.row_status is not None or args.reason_text is not None):\n            raise Refused(\"the ROW=STATUS and REASON operands belong to the triage verb alone.\")\n        if args.verb == \"session\":\n            if not args.model:\n                raise Refused(\"session needs --model <id>: name the model exactly as model-endpoints.yaml lists it.\")\n        elif args.model is not None or args.handover is not None:\n            raise Refused(\"--model and --handover belong to the session verb alone.\")\n       ",

          "citation": "docs/how-it-works.md::Who does what",
          "end_line": 95,
          "excerpt": "## Who does what\n\n**Claude is the orchestrator.** The Claude Code session runs each phase, calls\nthe runner, reads every result, decides on each finding, and writes the\nhandover. Other models do work inside a phase. They do not decide what happens\nnext.\n\nThe second development stage (Stage 2) hands some jobs to other models, and\nonly framework content goes to them:\n\n| Job | Who does it | Status on main |\n|---|---|---|\n| Orchestrate: run phases, decide findings, write the handover | Claude Code session | active |\n| Explore (phase 1) | GLM 5.3 Flash for a `spike` or `bounded` change; the research swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` one | active |\n| Draft spec, design and plan (2, 2b, 3) | Codex, OpenAI | active |\n| Review the spec (2a) | Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) | active |\n| Review loop (4b) | Pi, running the free and Flash swarms, then one paid model per round | active; until a clean round or a stop |\n| Implement (4) | GLM 5.3 Flash | active |\n| Repair the findings the orchestrator takes | Codex; Sonnet 5.5 after two failed checks | active |\n| Final review (6) | Codex, in a fresh read-only session | active |\n\n- **Codex** is OpenAI's coding model. The runner calls it.\n- **Pi** is the agent program the repository pins for the review loop\n  (ADR 0019). It sends the calls to **OpenCode Go**, which offers models from\n  several vendors. The operator is one, so the data recipient is one.\n- **Two read-only helpers** inside Claude Code: an explorer on Haiku 5.5 and a\n  reviewer on Opus 5.5, each with its model pinned\n  (`.claude/agents/explorer.md`, `reviewer.md`). They read and report; they\n  do not write.\n\nThe models behind each job are listed in `model-endpoints.yaml` and in\n`docs/WORKFLOW.md`, section 4. This table can lag behind them.\n\nEach provider needs your own access, set up on your machine. The repository\ntracks no credentials.\n\n",

          "citation": "README.md::Who checks what after a model call",
          "end_line": 166,
          "excerpt": "### Who checks what after a model call\n\nThe runner starts other models for named phases\n(`python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb> <change>`) and checks the result before it\ncommits anything. The check depends on the phase:\n\n- **Draft** (spec, design, plan): the locally runnable document gates,\n  outside the machine-wide verify lock.\n- **Implement**: a targeted check (the touched and linked tests and gates),\n  or `make verify` where that selection is not safe.\n- **Repair**: the red-first proof of each named test, then a targeted check:\n  the touched and linked test files and the gates their file kinds need. The\n  full `make verify` runs instead when that selection cannot cover the repair\n  safely, and always before the final review.\n- **Reviews** (spec review, review loop, final review): the model only reads;\n  the runner records its findings.\n\nA failed attempt goes to the next route with its diagnostics. The runner never\nmerges, never decides which finding is taken and never asks you anything.\nThose stay with the orchestrating agent and with you; so do the phase order,\nthe class, and the parallel-work rules below. Those rules are followed by the\nagent; no tool enforces them.\n\n",

          "citation": "docs/orchestration.md::What a lane is",
          "end_line": 39,
          "excerpt": "## What a lane is\n\n- **A lane is an ordered queue of changes.** Each item is one bead, one\n  branch and one worktree ([Working in parallel](../README.md#working-in-parallel)).\n  The queues are written down before a run starts. The night plan of\n  2026-10-28 is an example ([night plan](research/2026-10-28-night-run-plan.md)).\n- **One session orchestrates all of them.** It is the only tracker writer. It\n  starts the runner's verbs, decides review rows, writes the record and\n  commits. Models do the explore, draft, implement, repair and review work\n  through `scripts/stage2.py`.\n- **Disjoint files.** Only one lane changes a given hot file (for example\n  the runner, `scripts/stage2.py`). Two lanes never touch the same one.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "def _frontmatter_template(name: str, bead: str, owner: str, heute: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Frontmatter with every field from `plans_registry.REQUIRED` filled in.\n\n    Order and extra fields follow `plans/_README.md` — `supersedes` and\n    `superseded_by` are the only two fields that may be `null`.\n\n    `provenance: human-written` and **no** `produced_by` block: this file was\n    written by a deterministic call that a human issued. It used to say\n    `ai-drafted-reviewed` with\n    `produced_by: {kind: llm-session, name: unknown}` — a provenance that\n    nobody had at the time of writing, and that the provenance gate cannot\n    refute, because `plans/` permits exactly the two classes `human-written`\n    and `ai-drafted-reviewed`. Whoever fills the body with a language model\n    brings both up to date; the generated text says so.\n    \"\"\"\n    return f\"\"\"---\ntitle: \"Research — {name}\"\nstatus: draft\nimplementation_status: none\ndate: {heute}\nlast_reviewed: {heute}\nupdated: {heute}\nsupersedes: null\nsuperseded_by: null\nbead: {bead}\nowner: {owner}\nprovenance: human-written\ntags: [research]\n---\n\n\"\"\"\n",

          "end_line": 265,
          "excerpt": "def stamp(path: Path, today: date) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Set `updated:` to today by editing one line. True when the file changed.\n\n    Raises CannotStamp for a file that is not valid UTF-8: reading it with replacement\n    characters and writing it back would change bytes outside the line.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        text = path.read_bytes().decode(\"utf-8\")\n    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:\n        raise CannotStamp(f\"not valid UTF-8 ({exc.reason} at byte {exc.start})\") from exc\n    ergebnis = stamped(text, today)\n    if ergebnis == text:\n        return False\n    path.write_bytes(ergebnis.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n    return True\n",

          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::Repairing taken findings (repair)",
          "end_line": 2129,
          "excerpt": "### Repairing taken findings (repair)\n\n**The orchestrator decides, the verb repairs, the reviewer re-checks.** The\norchestrator writes `taken` or `rejected` on a phase-6 finding as into a loop\nrow, marks a finding no test can show `taken — not a test — <reason>` when\ntaking it, and starts the re-check afterwards: the loop's next round for loop\nrows, `review` for phase-6 findings. The verb starts no review of its own.\n\n`python3 scripts/stage2.py repair <change>` takes every taken row — of the\nloop record, of every released block and of every phase-6 table — to Codex\nin one guarded call, using the latest row of each ID across tables, with the\nactive loop record after findings history. Repeated IDs across tables are history.\nIt refuses while a row stands undecided or an ID is doubled within one table\nand either duplicate is taken; decided duplicates in passive history produce a\nnotice. Before the first call or write it checks every selected row's\n`Origin`, an older block's selected row included: a selected row of any\nblock — the loop record, a released block, any phase-6 table — whose\ncomplete trimmed cell is not `base` or `fix-r<N>` (N a positive whole\nnumber without a leading zero) refuses the repair, which names every\noffending row by ID and file (`loop.md` or `findings.md`), and the\norchestrator corrects the cell and starts the repair again. Released and\nsuperseded rows that no repair selects keep their exemption: history is\nnever swept for provenance, and no other verb gains this check.\n\nWhen the live record shadows a released copy in `findings.md`, repair fixes\nonly the live row and prints a notice. The released copy stays unchanged: an\noutstanding status there remains outstanding after a successful repair until\nthe next `release-loop` rewrites the released block from the record.\n\nBefore any model call, repair classifies every selected row by the repository\npaths its `Where` cell names, read the way the checkpoint's own protection\nreads them — case-insensitive prefixes from the committed provenance map and\nthe runner-held paths, with the change's own folder exemp",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "docs/WORKFLOW.md",
          "reference": "Repairing taken findings (repair)",
          "start_line": 1934,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": true
        }
      ],

          "end_line": 93,
          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "end_line": 301,
          "excerpt": "## Consumed-ladder amendment — the next step after the last stage, 2026-11-20\n\nThe maintainer decided on 2026-11-20, in the conversation of that day's run,\nthat a consumed ladder no longer stops the lane for a question. Decision 7\nsaid that exhausting the eligible stages with accepted findings stops and\nreports to the maintainer. In the night runs of 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20\nthat stop held two lanes (slip-counter, findings-per-model) until the\norchestrator applied the maintainer's answer by hand; a run's history cannot\nbe reset, so a new loop run was never an option.\n\nDecision 7 now reads, for this case: when every eligible stage of a run is\nconsumed, at least one review round completed in that run, and the last\nround was not clean, the loop ends without a further round and names the\nnext step. While a taken row of that round is open, the next step is the\nrepair of those rows; once every taken row is fixed, the next step is the\nphase-6 review, which checks that last repair through its full `make verify`\nand the reviewer's read of the whole diff. This holds also when the loop's\ndiff was cut at the line bound, because phase 6 reads the complete diff in\nthe worktree (`decisions.md` Q-5). When zero review rounds completed in the\nrun (total stage outage), the loop still stops and reports to the maintainer\ninstead of skipping phase 4b (`decisions.md` Q-4). No final-model repeat\nfollows, as before.\n\nUnchanged: the repair brake of decision 7 (two consecutive rounds each with\naccepted findings all caused by repairs, Origin `fix-r`, stop and go to the\nmaintainer) and every other stop of this ADR. The amendment changes where a\nconsumed ladder leads, not when the loop stops.\n\nThe runner carries the rule (house rule 9): `review-loop` ends such a run\nwith exit 0 and one line on standard output, `next: repair <change>` or\n`next: review <change>`, and does not start either verb itself (bead\ncoding-harness-hwll, change `ladder-next-step`, its `decisions.md` Q-2).\nUntil that change merges, the orchestrator applies this amendment by hand,\nas `AGENTS.md` states.\n",

          "excerpt": "def review_loop(root: Path, change: str, availability_reported: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"One round of phase 4b, until a round is clean (ADR 0021).\n\n    A fresh run discovers its free members through a forced live refresh and\n    pins the stage snapshot; every later call takes the run's next unconsumed\n    stage. The stops come before any stage: undecided or evidence-incomplete\n    rows first, then a clean previous round, then the repair brake (two\n    consecutive rounds whose accepted findings all begin `fix-r`), then spent\n    stages - each naming the round or the maintainer, and none reset by a\n    release or an edited configuration (ADR 0021, decision 9). One call\n    completes one round; a swarm's members run concurrently and merge into one\n    heading and one id series; an attempt whose every member failed completes\n    no round and consumes no stage.\n    \"\"\"\n    record = read_record(change, root)\n    if record is not None:\n        refusal = undecided_refusal(record_rows(record), \"decide them first\")\n        if refusal:\n            raise Refused(refusal)\n    findings_text = \"\"\n    findings_path = folder_of(root, change) / \"findings.md\"\n    if findings_path.exists():\n        findings_text = findings_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    refusal = origin_refusal(record, findings_text)\n    if refusal:\n        raise Refused(refusal)\n    if record is not None:\n        refusal = released_overlap_refusal(record, findings_text)\n        if refusal:\n            raise Refused(refusal)\n    if record is None:\n        refusal = lost_record_refusal(change, root, findings_text)\n        if refusal:\n            raise Refused(refusal)\n    # The snapshot before the stops: a released block without the runner's snapshot is refused here,\n    # never read as a finished run (DL-A-2 of the deep review).\n    state = None if restarted_fresh(record, findings_text) else read_state(record, findings_text)",

          "end_line": 423,
          "excerpt": "### Artefact lifecycle\n\n```\nplans/specs/<capability>/spec.md          LIVING      — what should hold today\nplans/changes/<name>/                     ACTIVE      — one change in flight\nplans/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>/  HISTORICAL  — closed\ndocs/adr/NNNN-title.md                    PERMANENT   — append-only\n```\n\nTwo separate status fields: `status` moves when the project decides;\n`implementation_status` when the code moves. One field for both cannot say\nwhether an accepted spec is still unbuilt or whether built code rests on a\nwithdrawn spec — and those are exactly the interesting cases.\n\nOn close: the delta into the living capability spec, permanent architectural\ndecisions as an ADR, the rest into the archive. **An implemented feature spec\ndoes not stay as a living document** — the code and the git history are the\ntruth. Details in [`plans/_README.md`](../plans/_README.md).\n\nThe **rule against making a second one** stands verbatim in `AGENTS.md`, because\nan agent does not necessarily read `plans/_README.md`: before an artefact is\ncreated, search with `rg` first; where one exists, it is updated. `make\nstaleness` checks the consequences — missing frontmatter, contradictory status,\ndone and never archived, one-sided supersession.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "def stamp(path: Path, today: date) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Set `updated:` to today by editing one line. True when the file changed.\n\n    Raises CannotStamp for a file that is not valid UTF-8: reading it with replacement\n    characters and writing it back would change bytes outside the line.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        text = path.read_bytes().decode(\"utf-8\")\n    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:\n        raise CannotStamp(f\"not valid UTF-8 ({exc.reason} at byte {exc.start})\") from exc\n    ergebnis = stamped(text, today)\n    if ergebnis == text:\n        return False\n    path.write_bytes(ergebnis.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n    return True\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "excerpt": "## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. When independent checks use the default setting, at most two protected admissions share the machine across repositories and worktrees, and both available slots can be reserved.\n   *Refuted by:* a third admission runs, or the eligible head waiter cannot reserve an otherwise free slot within two queue poll intervals (0.5 seconds at the default interval).\n   *Basis:* `decisions.md#Q-1`.\n\n2. When an independent entry requests capacity `1` or `2` through `HARNESS_VERIFY_SLOTS` (default `2`), effective capacity is the minimum of the settings of all live updated holders and the head live waiter; an older waiter counts as `1` and requires exclusive access.\n   *Refuted by:* a `1` holder shares capacity, a head `1` waiter enters before all holders drain, or two `2` entries cannot use both free slots.\n\n   Local child processes receive the setting when present; the foreign-model environment allow-list remains closed to `HARNESS_*` variables.\n   *Basis:* `decisions.md#Q-1`.\n\n3. If an independent entry has `HARNESS_VERIFY_SLOTS` set to anything other than the exact strings `1` or `2`, it refuses before protected work with a diagnostic naming the setting.\n   *Refuted by:* an empty, padded, `02`, `+2`, fractional or other invalid value starts work, or a valid inherited descendant is refused because of that setting.\n   *Basis:* `decisions.md#Q-1`.\n\n4. While independent live checks wait, the earliest registered live waiter, including an older checkout waiting exclusively, has first claim on capacity free under criterion 2.\n   *Refuted by:* a later waiter overtakes a live earlier waiter, a dead waiter blocks progress, or the eligible head waiter cannot reserve a free slot under the effective capacity within two queue poll intervals (0.5 seconds at the default interval).",

          "citation": "docs/adr/0021-review-swarms-until-clean.md::Consumed-ladder amendment — the next step after the last stage, 2026-11-20",
          "end_line": 301,
          "excerpt": "## Consumed-ladder amendment — the next step after the last stage, 2026-11-20\n\nThe maintainer decided on 2026-11-20, in the conversation of that day's run,\nthat a consumed ladder no longer stops the lane for a question. Decision 7\nsaid that exhausting the eligible stages with accepted findings stops and\nreports to the maintainer. In the night runs of 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20\nthat stop held two lanes (slip-counter, findings-per-model) until the\norchestrator applied the maintainer's answer by hand; a run's history cannot\nbe reset, so a new loop run was never an option.\n\nDecision 7 now reads, for this case: when every eligible stage of a run is\nconsumed, at least one review round completed in that run, and the last\nround was not clean, the loop ends without a further round and names the\nnext step. While a taken row of that round is open, the next step is the\nrepair of those rows; once every taken row is fixed, the next step is the\nphase-6 review, which checks that last repair through its full `make verify`\nand the reviewer's read of the whole diff. This holds also when the loop's\ndiff was cut at the line bound, because phase 6 reads the complete diff in\nthe worktree (`decisions.md` Q-5). When zero review rounds completed in the\nrun (total stage outage), the loop still stops and reports to the maintainer\ninstead of skipping phase 4b (`decisions.md` Q-4). No final-model repeat\nfollows, as before.\n\nUnchanged: the repair brake of decision 7 (two consecutive rounds each with\naccepted findings all caused by repairs, Origin `fix-r`, stop and go to the\nmaintainer) and every other stop of this ADR. The amendment changes where a\nconsumed ladder leads, not when the loop stops.\n\nThe runner carries the rule (house rule 9): `review-loop` ends such a run\nwith exit 0 and one line on standard output, `next: repair <change>` or\n`next: review <change>`, and does not start either verb itself (bead\ncoding-harness-hwll, change `ladder-next-step`, its `decisions.md` Q-2).\nUntil that change merges, the orchestrator applies this amendment by hand,\nas `AGENTS.md` states.\n",

        },

          "citation": "AGENTS.md::The workflow in one screen",

          "excerpt": "## The workflow in one screen\n\n| # | Phase | Artifact | Gate |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Explore | `plans/changes/<name>/research.md` | — |\n| 1a | Interview | `decisions.md` | the class minimums met — feature ≥ 3 · ADR change ≥ 5 (feature with ADR: 5 total) · spike 3 topics or reasoned skip · bounded 1 or reasoned skip — gate `interview-minimums` |\n| 2 | Spec | `spec.md` | validator green, no open `[DECISION]` |\n| 2a | Spec-Review *(not for a spike)* | lines for `findings.md`, dimension SPEC | a current review of the spec, no open `[AMBIGUITY]`; at most three spec-review rounds — the final draft after round three needs no new review, a fourth round only by a recorded maintainer answer |\n| 2b | Design *(by class)* | `design.md` | validator green; an ADR draft when `architectural` |\n| 3 | Plan | `plan.md` | validator green |\n| 4 | Implement | code + tests | `make verify` green |\n| 4b | Review loop *(stage 2)* | loop rows, into `findings.md` after the phase-6 verdict | rounds until a clean round — the free swarm, the Flash swarm, then the paid ladder (ADR 0021); a targeted check after each runner repair and each orchestrator hand repair, the full `make verify` before phase 6 |\n| 5 | Verify | test output as evidence | stop-hook blocks on a red tree |\n| 6 | Review | `findings.md` | no open BLOCKER — `[DIVERGENT]` counts as BLOCKER |\n| 7 | Commit | pull request | CI green |\n\n**Stage 2** (framework content, ADR 0007 as amended by ADR 0011 and ADR 0016): a foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py`, which runs the leak check before every call. Codex drafts spec, design and plan (`draft <change>`; GLM 5.3 after two failed attempts) and reviews 6; Opus 5.5 reviews 2a (`spec-review <change>`); the review loop (4b) runs on OpenCode Go through Pi until a clean round (ADR 0021): round 1 is the free swarm, the models the `free_stage` rule selects from a forced live catalog refresh, on the implementation diff alone with no tools; round 2 is the Flash swarm, up to three cheapest reachable admitted paid models in parallel; then one id of the `opencode-go` entry's `modelle` set per round, cheapest first: the runner orders it by the declared `",

          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::The runner is the only way",
          "end_line": 1506,
          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept; one retry after the configured pause, then the declared\n  fallback through Pi; at most three rounds (\"The spec review before the plan\n  card\").\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`. On every route it first refuses, before any model\n  starts, a refused class or a `bounded`, `feature` or `architectural` change\n  without a current spec review free of open `[AMBIGUITY]` rows.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuse",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"One runner with stage barriers and provider queues\", because\nit keeps the established entry point while making boundaries and handoff\ncheckable.\n\n1. `stage2.py explore` dispatches features and architectural changes to the\n   swarm, bounded/spike to GLM Flash; explicit Stage-1 fallback remains Haiku\n   5.5 with its reason. Early research/spec/argument classes must agree.\n   Swarm research headers require an explicit neighbours list; [] is valid,\n   while a missing/null/non-list key refuses with exit 2 and a repair message.\n2. Finder step 0 uses the three repository seats as independent\n   locators; Opus 5.5 merges code, rules/ADRs, tests/gates and neighbour lists.\n   The merged finder keys are their exact deduplicated category/reference\n   union with all origins/reasons; extra or missing keys fail preparation.\n   Runner resolution against scratch frozen bytes marks unresolved entries\n   without granting topic scope, then inserts all given neighbours as given.\n   Finder suggestions remain marked rather than silently accepted.\n   Eligible neighbour specs have three forms: plans/changes/<name>/spec.md\n   (one segment other than archive),\n   plans/changes/archive/<YYYY-MM-DD-name>/spec.md, and\n   plans/specs/<capability>/spec.md, excluding the change's own spec. Resolved\n   neighbour-category artifacts inside those folders map to the frozen spec\n   if present, retaining every finder key. Own-change entries are self with\n   no relation/gap; other resolved entries are no-spec with named gaps.\n   Given paths outside those forms or the own spec refuse with exit 2;\n   eligible given paths must exist in frozen bytes.\n3. Topics 1–8 cover code/reuse, callers/interfaces, rules/class, architecture,\n   neighbours, history/volatility, tests/gates and risks; each uses the\n   three repository seats on identical briefs, perspectives and report\n   template.\n   After map merge the runner collects topic 6's local frozen-HEAD history:\n   up to ten most recent commits per resolved mapped path, with full hash,\n   UTC author date, subject, body capped at 4,000 characters with truncation\n   marked, and touched mapped paths. Older history is not read. Only topic 6\n   receives it; a full packet hash resolves to that record, but a reachable\n   hash outside the packet or PR/bead id alone is unsupported. No network or\n   tracker is read; collection failure prevents topics and exits 1 incomplete.\n4. Topics 9–11 cover best practice, existing tools/standards and public failure\n   reports. Each uses the three online seats through Pi with only the\n   filtered Opus sentence, fixed questions and public sources.\n   In addition, every eligible Go chat model ending `-free`, selected from a\n   live-fetched Pi Go overlay with declared include/exclude lists, works each\n   online topic on the same brief. No Zen provider, OpenCode CLI, fixed free\n   roster or substitution for the online seats. Dynamic free\n   permission applies to public-only research, never private roles. Select only\n   fresh-Pi text-input chat entries with exact matching models.dev\n   opencode-go.models keys, with a present id field equal to the key,\n   boolean tool_call true and status not deprecated.\n   Missing/negative support, missing metadata, deprecated, non-chat and\n   baseline-only entries are excluded with reasons. Unavailable/unreadable\n   models.dev excludes all free candidates as capability-unavailable N=0,\n   retaining required slots; this is distinct from a measured empty eligible set.\n   Both sources are dated/digested. Pi refresh failure exits 1 before all\n   models; Pi's absent capability field is expected, never a fallback trigger. These free\n   seats are best-effort: failure is named, never hidden or substituted, and\n   does not alone invalidate the 39 required contributions.\n   Missing/non-object provider/models, non-object root, invalid JSON,\n   non-200/request failure or duplicate claimed ids are document-level\n   capability-unavailable. On every route it first refuses, before any model\n  starts, a refused class or a `bounded`, `feature` or `architectural` change\n  without a current spec review free of open `[AMBIGUITY]` rows.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`.
