          "excerpt": "def clear_written(root: Path, plan: Path) -> list[int]:\n    \"\"\"Remove `not yet written` from every ledger entry whose named test exists; return their numbers.\n\n    The marker is derivable from the tree, so the stage-2 runner clears it before its own `make\n    verify`, as it renders the index and stamps the dates (bead coding-harness-7g6h). An entry whose\n    file or function is missing keeps its marker, and lines in a fence are never touched. Every other\n    byte of the plan stays as it was.\n    \"\"\"\n    text, _ = read(plan)\n    if text is None:\n        return []\n    raw = text.split(\"\\n\")\n    lines = _lines(text)\n    # A fence under the ledger heading still belongs to the section; its lines are examples (P239-1).\n    fenced = _fenced(lines)\n    cleared: list[int] = []\n    for section in ledger_sections(lines):\n        for number, line in section:\n            if fenced[number - 1]:\n                continue\n            entry = parse_entry(line, number)\n            if entry is None or entry.kind != \"not yet written\":\n                continue\n            found, _ = read(root / entry.path)\n            if found is None or not _defined(found, entry.function):\n                continue\n            raw[number - 1] = raw[number - 1].replace(\": not yet written \", \": \", 1)\n            cleared.append(entry.number)\n    if cleared:\n        plan.write_text(\"\\n\".join(raw), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    return cleared\n",

          "excerpt": "def repair_doctrine_problems(workflow: str, agents: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 30: the doctrine names the verb, routes the repair, and gives the Status to the orchestrator.\"\"\"\n    found = []\n    four = flat(section(workflow, \"## 4 · \"))\n    if \"Eleven verbs exist\" in four or \"Thirteen verbs exist\" not in four:\n        found.append(\"section 4 does not say thirteen verbs\")\n    if \"- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding\" not in workflow:\n        found.append(\"the verb list has no repair bullet\")\n    if \"| Repair after 4b and 6 | **gpt-6.1-terra** |\" not in workflow:\n        found.append(\"the routing table has no repair row\")\n    if \"### Repairing taken findings (repair)\" not in workflow:\n        found.append(\"the repair subsection is missing\")\n    loop = flat(section(workflow, \"### The review loop\"))\n    if \"The orchestrator writes\" not in loop or \"verb repairs the taken rows\" not in loop:\n        found.append(\"the loop section does not give the Status to the orchestrator and the repair to the verb\")\n    fixing = flat(section(workflow, \"### Repairing taken findings\"))\n    for needle in (\"python3 scripts/stage2.py repair <change>\", \"Red first\", \"Broke a test\"):\n        if needle not in fixing:\n            found.append(f\"the repair subsection lacks '{needle}'\")\n    one = flat(agents)\n    if \"Codex repairs the findings the orchestrator takes\" not in one:\n        found.append(\"AGENTS.md does not name the repair on Codex\")\n    if \"explore, draft, implement and repair do not\" not in one:\n        found.append(\"AGENTS.md does not count repair and draft among the verbs without reviews by class\")\n    return found\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_the_makefile_runs_what_the_one_list_runs() -> None:\n    \"\"\"W-6: nothing pinned the Makefile, although it duplicates gate commands verbatim.\n\n    `make test` and `make staleness` repeat what stands in `ci.yml` as a gate.\n    If the step there changes its flags, the two drift apart silently — and\n    being green locally while CI is red is exactly the state `verify_all.sh`\n    argues against by holding no list of its own.\n\n    What is compared is the **whole recipe line**, not a substring.       ],
      "statement": "Verb registration is partly derived and partly hard-coded: `VERBS` maps names to handlers, `_run` derives its whitelist with `known = sorted([*VERBS, \"session\", \"prepare-explore\"])` and ends with `else: VERBS[args.verb](root, change)`, so a handler with that signature is reachable from `VERBS` alone. Option ownership is not derived: `--stage2-off` is refused unless the verb is explore/implement/repair, `--class` only for explore/prepare-explore, `--availability-reported` only for explore/review-loop, `--model`/`--handover` only for session. The optional `--stage2-off` value can swallow the change name, detected only when that value happens to be an existing folder under `plans/changes/`. The parametrised refusal test sweeps every name in `stage2.VERBS` with missing, `..` and `a/b` changes."
    },

          "excerpt": "def implement(root: Path, change: str, stage2_off: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 4: Flash, one Flash repair and Sonnet fallback, checked and committed by the runner.\"\"\"\n    first = SONNET if stage2_off is not None else GLM_FLASH\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, first, required=(\"plan.md\",))\n    allowed = {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\n    refuse_preexisting(root, allowed)\n    baseline = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    time_log(ctx.plan)  # Require the initial time heading before a model call starts.\n    ignored_before = ignored_snapshot(root)\n    # The class statement and the current spec review (bead coding-harness-ttic): one admission\n    # for every route, checked before a model starts; a spike reaches the existing checks.\n    admission = review_admission(root, change)\n    if admission.class_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.class_problem)\n    if admission.review_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.review_problem)\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        key = read_secret(\"GLM_KEY\")\n        if key is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"GLM_KEY is not in the secrets file {secrets_path()}.\")\n        routes = [\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash\", None),\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash-repair\", \"first Flash post-run check failed\"),\n            (SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", \"two Flash post-run checks failed\"),\n        ]\n    else:\n        key = None\n        routes = [(SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", stage2_off)]\n    standing: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    def snapshot() -> str:\n        text = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        standing[\"text\"] = text\n        return text\n\n    def check(_answer: str) -> list[str]:\n        # The implementing model writes code, never loop state. The runner puts findings.md back\n        # before this check (spec, criterion 8), so a model edit alone never fails here; the\n        # comparison stays as the guard that the restore held (review row L3-2).\n        now = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        problem = findings_body_problem(standing.get(\"text\", \"\"), now)\n        return [problem] if problem else []\n\n    run_attempts(\n        ctx,\n        \"implement\",\n        routes,\n        lambda diagnostics, _endpoint, inputs: implementation_prompt(ctx, baseline, diagnostics, inputs),\n        baseline,\n        key,\n        ignored_before,\n        commit_message=f\"feat({change}): implement accepted plan\",\n        closing=(\n            \"implementation post-run checks failed after the allowed attempts; why each attempt failed and \"\n            f\"the files it changed: {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\"\n        ),\n        answer_check=check,\n        snapshot_findings=snapshot,\n        restore_findings=lambda text: restore_work_input(root, ctx.findings, text.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        # Every model route's post-run check is targeted when the coverage is safe (bead\n        # coding-harness-0swp): the covered initial, retry and stage-1 routes alike. New production\n        # code without a reachable test refuses before any test runs or a fallback is admitted.\n        verify_mode=\"targeted\",\n        new_file_guard=True,\n    )\n",

          "end_line": 301,
          "excerpt": "## Consumed-ladder amendment — the next step after the last stage, 2026-11-20\n\nThe maintainer decided on 2026-11-20, in the conversation of that day's run,\nthat a consumed ladder no longer stops the lane for a question. Decision 7\nsaid that exhausting the eligible stages with accepted findings stops and\nreports to the maintainer. In the night runs of 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20\nthat stop held two lanes (slip-counter, findings-per-model) until the\norchestrator applied the maintainer's answer by hand; a run's history cannot\nbe reset, so a new loop run was never an option.\n\nDecision 7 now reads, for this case: when every eligible stage of a run is\nconsumed, at least one review round completed in that run, and the last\nround was not clean, the loop ends without a further round and names the\nnext step. While a taken row of that round is open, the next step is the\nrepair of those rows; once every taken row is fixed, the next step is the\nphase-6 review, which checks that last repair through its full `make verify`\nand the reviewer's read of the whole diff. This holds also when the loop's\ndiff was cut at the line bound, because phase 6 reads the complete diff in\nthe worktree (`decisions.md` Q-5). When zero review rounds completed in the\nrun (total stage outage), the loop still stops and reports to the maintainer\ninstead of skipping phase 4b (`decisions.md` Q-4). No final-model repeat\nfollows, as before.\n\nUnchanged: the repair brake of decision 7 (two consecutive rounds each with\naccepted findings all caused by repairs, Origin `fix-r`, stop and go to the\nmaintainer) and every other stop of this ADR. The amendment changes where a\nconsumed ladder leads, not when the loop stops.\n\nThe runner carries the rule (house rule 9): `review-loop` ends such a run\nwith exit 0 and one line on standard output, `next: repair <change>` or\n`next: review <change>`, and does not start either verb itself (bead\ncoding-harness-hwll, change `ladder-next-step`, its `decisions.md` Q-2).\nUntil that change merges, the orchestrator applies this amendment by hand,\nas `AGENTS.md` states.\n",

          "excerpt": "def review_loop(root: Path, change: str, availability_reported: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"One round of phase 4b, until a round is clean (ADR 0021).\n\n    A fresh run discovers its free members through a forced live refresh and\n    pins the stage snapshot; every later call takes the run's next unconsumed\n    stage. The stops come before any stage: undecided or evidence-incomplete\n    rows first, then a clean previous round, then the repair brake (two\n    consecutive rounds whose accepted findings all begin `fix-r`), then spent\n    stages - each naming the round or the maintainer, and none reset by a\n    release or an edited configuration (ADR 0021, decision 9). One call\n    completes one round; a swarm's members run concurrently and merge into one\n    heading and one id series; an attempt whose every member failed completes\n    no round and consumes no stage.\n    \"\"\"\n    record = read_record(change, root)\n    if record is not None:\n        refusal = undecided_refusal(record_rows(record), \"decide them first\")\n        if refusal:\n            raise Refused(refusal)\n    findings_text = \"\"\n    findings_path = folder_of(root, change) / \"findings.md\"\n    if findings_path.exists():\n        findings_text = findings_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    refusal = origin_refusal(record, findings_text)\n    if refusal:\n        raise Refused(refusal)\n    if record is not None:\n        refusal = released_overlap_refusal(record, findings_text)\n        if refusal:\n            raise Refused(refusal)\n    if record is None:\n        refusal = lost_record_refusal(change, root, findings_text)\n        if refusal:\n            raise Refused(refusal)\n    # The snapshot before the stops: a released block without the runner's snapshot is refused here,\n    # never read as a finished run (DL-A-2 of the deep review).\n    state = None if restarted_fresh(record, findings_text) else read_state(record, findings_text)",

          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept; one retry after the configured pause, then the declared\n  fallback through Pi; at most three rounds (\"The spec review before the plan\n  card\").\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`. On every route it first refuses, before any model\n  starts, a refused class or a `bounded`, `feature` or `architectural` change\n  without a current spec review free of open `[AMBIGUITY]` rows.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuse",

          "excerpt": "def implement(root: Path, change: str, stage2_off: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 4: Flash, one Flash repair and Sonnet fallback, checked and committed by the runner.\"\"\"\n    first = SONNET if stage2_off is not None else GLM_FLASH\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, first, required=(\"plan.md\",))\n    allowed = {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\n    refuse_preexisting(root, allowed)\n    baseline = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    time_log(ctx.plan)  # Require the initial time heading before a model call starts.\n    ignored_before = ignored_snapshot(root)\n    # The class statement and the current spec review (bead coding-harness-ttic): one admission\n    # for every route, checked before a model starts; a spike reaches the existing checks.\n    admission = review_admission(root, change)\n    if admission.class_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.class_problem)\n    if admission.review_problem is not None:\n        raise Refused(admission.review_problem)\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        key = read_secret(\"GLM_KEY\")\n        if key is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"GLM_KEY is not in the secrets file {secrets_path()}.\")\n        routes = [\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash\", None),\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash-repair\", \"first Flash post-run check failed\"),\n            (SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", \"two Flash post-run checks failed\"),\n        ]\n    else:\n        key = None\n        routes = [(SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", stage2_off)]\n    standing: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    def snapshot() -> str:\n        text = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        standing[\"text\"] = text\n        return text\n\n    def check(_answer: str) -> list[str]:\n        # The implementing model writes code, never loop state. The runner puts findings.md back\n        # before this check (spec, criterion 8), so a model edit alone never fails here; the\n        # comparison stays as the guard that the restore held (review row L3-2).\n        now = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        problem = findings_body_problem(standing.get(\"text\", \"\"), now)\n        return [problem] if problem else []\n\n    run_attempts(\n        ctx,\n        \"implement\",\n        routes,\n        lambda diagnostics, _endpoint, inputs: implementation_prompt(ctx, baseline, diagnostics, inputs),\n        baseline,\n        key,\n        ignored_before,\n        commit_message=f\"feat({change}): implement accepted plan\",\n        closing=(\n            \"implementation post-run checks failed after the allowed attempts; why each attempt failed and \"\n            f\"the files it changed: {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\"\n        ),\n        answer_check=check,\n        snapshot_findings=snapshot,\n        restore_findings=lambda text: restore_work_input(root, ctx.findings, text.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        # Every model route's post-run check is targeted when the coverage is safe (bead\n        # coding-harness-0swp): the covered initial, retry and stage-1 routes alike. New production\n        # code without a reachable test refuses before any test runs or a fallback is admitted.\n        verify_mode=\"targeted\",\n        new_file_guard=True,\n    )\n",

          "excerpt": "def spec_review_inventory(root: Path) -> int:\n    \"\"\"`--spec-review-inventory`: the morning inventory of missing spec reviews (spec criteria 16-17).\n\n    Every non-archived change folder with a `spec.md` - implemented changes included - is\n    measured with the same admission implement faces. Groups: changes whose class is missing,\n    invalid or disagreeing; changes failing the review check, the three-round exception\n    applied; and changes whose newest current qualifying review is a fallback, named for an\n    Opus re-check in the next day session - the re-check replaces the fallback review in the\n    same round. Spikes and folders without a spec stand outside. A change that cannot be read\n    is reported, never silently omitted: any error while measuring one change - a git launch\n    failure included - names that change in a group of its own, and the list goes on (review row L4-2).\n    \"\"\"\n    base = root / \"plans\" / \"changes\"\n    class_refused: list[str] = []\n    review_refused: list[str] = []\n    rechecks: list[str] = []\n    unmeasured: list[str] = []\n    folders = []\n    if base.is_dir():\n        folders = sorted(entry for entry in base.iterdir() if entry.is_dir() and entry.name != \"archive\")\n    for folder in folders:\n        name = folder.name\n        if not (folder / \"spec.md\").is_file():\n            continue\n        try:\n            admission = review_admission(root, name)\n        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - one change's failure is reported, the list goes on\n            unmeasured.append(f\"{name} ({type(error).__name__}: {error})\")\n            continue\n        if admission.class_problem is not None:\n            class_refused.append(f\"{name} ({admission.class_problem})\")\n        if admission.review_problem is not None:\n            review_refused.append(f\"{name} ({admission.review_problem})\")\n        if admission.recheck:\n            rechecks.append(name)\n    print(\"Spec-review inventory — changes without a current spec review:\")\n    if class_refused:\n        print(\"\\nClass refused (missing, invalid or disagreeing):\")\n        print(\"\\n\".join(f\"- {line}\" for line in class_refused))\n    if review_refused:\n        print(\"\\nReview missing, unreadable, stale or ambiguous:\")\n        print(\"\\n\".join(f\"- {line}\" for line in review_refused))\n    if rechecks:\n        print(\"\\nFallback review to re-check with Opus in the next day session (same round):\")\n        print(\"\\n\".join(f\"- {line}\" for line in rechecks))\n    if unmeasured:\n        print(\"\\nNot measured (an error while measuring the change):\")\n        print(\"\\n\".join(f\"- {line}\" for line in unmeasured))\n    if not (class_refused or review_refused or rechecks or unmeasured):\n        print(\"\\nNone. Every change with a spec holds a current qualifying review.\")\n    return 0\n",

          "citation": "scripts/harness.py::main",
          "end_line": 524,
          "excerpt": "def main(argv: list[str] | None = None, *, ask: Ask = input, out: Out = print, today: date | None = None) -> int:\n    args = parser().parse_args(argv)\n    root: Path = args.root.resolve()\n    try:\n        if args.verb == \"time-log\":\n            return time_log(root, args, out=out, today=today or date.today())\n        given: dict[str, Any] = {name: getattr(args, name) for name in RECORDING}\n        if any(v is not None for v in given.values()):\n            flags = {name: \"--\" + name.replace(\"_\", \"-\") for name in RECORDING}\n            absent = [flags[n] for n, v in given.items() if v is None or not str(v).strip()]\n            if absent:\n                raise Refused(\n                    f\"recording an answer needs all four of {', '.join(flags.values())}; missing or blank: {', '.join(absent)}\"\n                )\n        role = answering_role(root)\n        message = message_path(root)\n        day = today or date.today()\n        if given[\"change\"] is not None:\n            return record_adr(\n                root,\n                given[\"change\"],\n                given[\"answer\"],\n                given[\"reason\"],\n                given[\"stated_in\"],\n                out=out,\n                today=day,\n                role=role,\n                message_path=message,\n            )\n        if not sys.stdin.isatty():\n            raise Refused(\n                \"run this yourself in a terminal — the questions are for the maintainer to answer; \"\n                \"an answer stated elsewhere is recorded with --change, --answer, --reason and --stated-in\"\n            )\n        return decide_adr(root, ask=ask, out=out, today=day, role=role, message_path=message)\n    except Refused as exc:\n        out(f\"refused: {exc}\")\n        out(\"Nothing was written.\")\n        return 2\n",

          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed rep",

          "end_line": 265,
          "excerpt": "def stamp(path: Path, today: date) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Set `updated:` to today by editing one line. True when the file changed.\n\n    Raises CannotStamp for a file that is not valid UTF-8: reading it with replacement\n    characters and writing it back would change bytes outside the line.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        text = path.read_bytes().decode(\"utf-8\")\n    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:\n        raise CannotStamp(f\"not valid UTF-8 ({exc.reason} at byte {exc.start})\") from exc\n    ergebnis = stamped(text, today)\n    if ergebnis == text:\n        return False\n    path.write_bytes(ergebnis.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n    return True\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/check_frontmatter_current.py",
          "reference": "stamp",

          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::### Artefact lifecycle",
          "end_line": 423,
          "excerpt": "### Artefact lifecycle\n\n```\nplans/specs/<capability>/spec.md          LIVING      — what should hold today\nplans/changes/<name>/                     ACTIVE      — one change in flight\nplans/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>/  HISTORICAL  — closed\ndocs/adr/NNNN-title.md                    PERMANENT   — append-only\n```\n\nTwo separate status fields: `status` moves when the project decides;\n`implementation_status` when the code moves. One field for both cannot say\nwhether an accepted spec is still unbuilt or whether built code rests on a\nwithdrawn spec — and those are exactly the interesting cases.\n\nOn close: the delta into the living capability spec, permanent architectural\ndecisions as an ADR, the rest into the archive. **An implemented feature spec\ndoes not stay as a living document** — the code and the git history are the\ntruth. Details in [`plans/_README.md`](../plans/_README.md).\n\nThe **rule against making a second one** stands verbatim in `AGENTS.md`, because\nan agent does not necessarily read `plans/_README.md`: before an artefact is\ncreated, search with `rg` first; where one exists, it is updated. `make\nstaleness` checks the consequences — missing frontmatter, contradictory status,\ndone and never archived, one-sided supersession.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "docs/WORKFLOW.md",
          "reference": "### Artefact lifecycle",
          "start_line": 399,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        }
      ],
      "statement": "Lifecycle header writes have silent no-op edge cases an advance verb would touch: `stamp` returns the text unchanged when the frontmatter block is absent or when more than one `updated:` line exists, and raises CannotStamp only for non-UTF-8 input; archiving edits exactly the four fields `status`, `implementation_status`, `updated`, `last_reviewed` and preserves the rest byte for byte. The two-field design (status vs implementation_status) is doctrine precisely because one field cannot say whether an accepted spec is unbuilt — a phase-moving writer that gets these fields wrong produces exactly the drift `make staleness` checks for."
    }

          "excerpt": "## Consumed-ladder amendment — the next step after the last stage, 2026-11-20\n\nThe maintainer decided on 2026-11-20, in the conversation of that day's run,\nthat a consumed ladder no longer stops the lane for a question. Decision 7\nsaid that exhausting the eligible stages with accepted findings stops and\nreports to the maintainer. In the night runs of 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-20\nthat stop held two lanes (slip-counter, findings-per-model) until the\norchestrator applied the maintainer's answer by hand; a run's history cannot\nbe reset, so a new loop run was never an option.\n\nDecision 7 now reads, for this case: when every eligible stage of a run is\nconsumed, at least one review round completed in that run, and the last\nround was not clean, the loop ends without a further round and names the\nnext step. While a taken row of that round is open, the next step is the\nrepair of those rows; once every taken row is fixed, the next step is the\nphase-6 review, which checks that last repair through its full `make verify`\nand the reviewer's read of the whole diff. This holds also when the loop's\ndiff was cut at the line bound, because phase 6 reads the complete diff in\nthe worktree (`decisions.md` Q-5). When zero review rounds completed in the\nrun (total stage outage), the loop still stops and reports to the maintainer\ninstead of skipping phase 4b (`decisions.md` Q-4). No final-model repeat\nfollows, as before.\n\nUnchanged: the repair brake of decision 7 (two consecutive rounds each with\naccepted findings all caused by repairs, Origin `fix-r`, stop and go to the\nmaintainer) and every other stop of this ADR. The amendment changes where a\nconsumed ladder leads, not when the loop stops.\n\nThe runner carries the rule (house rule 9): `review-loop` ends such a run\nwith exit 0 and one line on standard output, `next: repair <change>` or\n`next: review <change>`, and does not start either verb itself (bead\ncoding-harness-hwll, change `ladder-next-step`, its `decisions.md` Q-2).\nUntil that change merges, the orchestrator applies this amendment by hand,\nas `AGENTS.md` states.\n",

          "excerpt": "def review_loop(root: Path, change: str, availability_reported: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"One round of phase 4b, until a round is clean (ADR 0021).\n\n    A fresh run discovers its free members through a forced live refresh and\n    pins the stage snapshot; every later call takes the run's next unconsumed\n    stage. The stops come before any stage: undecided or evidence-incomplete\n    rows first, then a clean previous round, then the repair brake (two\n    consecutive rounds whose accepted findings all begin `fix-r`), then spent\n    stages - each naming the round or the maintainer, and none reset by a\n    release or an edited configuration (ADR 0021, decision 9). One call\n    completes one round; a swarm's members run concurrently and merge into one\n    heading and one id series; an attempt whose every member failed completes\n    no round and consumes no stage.\n    \"\"\"\n    record = read_record(change, root)\n    if record is not None:\n        refusal = undecided_refusal(record_rows(record), \"decide them first\")\n        if refusal:\n            raise Refused(refusal)\n    findings_text = \"\"\n    findings_path = folder_of(root, change) / \"findings.md\"\n    if findings_path.exists():\n        findings_text = findings_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    refusal = origin_refusal(record, findings_text)\n    if refusal:\n        raise Refused(refusal)\n    if record is not None:\n        refusal = released_overlap_refusal(record, findings_text)\n        if refusal:\n            raise Refused(refusal)\n    if record is None:\n        refusal = lost_record_refusal(change, root, findings_text)\n        if refusal:\n            raise Refused(refusal)\n    # The snapshot before the stops: a released block without the runner's snapshot is refused here,\n    # never read as a finished run (DL-A-2 of the deep review).\n    state = None if restarted_fresh(record, findings_text) else read_state(record, findings_text)",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

As a feature it owes ADR-question and interview records, and research-handoff turns red once a spec exists without a complete v2 run (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/3/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C3, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/7/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C4, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/6/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C2).",
      "The ADR 0021 hand-back form (name the next step, start nothing, exit 0) already matches the external guidance to make the resulting state legible and not guess the successor (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/2/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C6, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C2, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C6)."
    ],
    "architecture_comparison": "The repository's architecture has one runner path for foreign models (stage2.py) and a model-free harness.py CLI, and both refuse without writing (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/1/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C2, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/8/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C1). House rule 9 requires one entry point and one writer per action (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/4/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C2). The documentation leaves the next step to the orchestrator, with no tool enforcing phase order (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/4/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C3). Phase order exists only as prose, while the status fields are a closed two-field vocabulary with several writers (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/1/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C5, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/1/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C6). The runner holds a per-change record lock for the loop verbs and performs no tracker write (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/8/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C3, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/4/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C7). stage2.py stays in this repository, while harness.py travels with the kit (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/2/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C7). An advance verb therefore fits only inside one of the two existing paths. In stage2 it inherits the sweep, recognition, lock and admission but needs doctrine-count and fixed-list edits (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/7/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C2, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/7/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C3). In harness.py it inherits the plan writer and the stamp callback but travels into instances. Two points remain contested. One is whether a verb that starts the next verb contradicts ADR 0021 (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/4/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C4 against bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/3/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C7). The other is how many places in stage2.py a new verb must touch (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/1/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C1 against bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/8/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C2).",
    "assumptions": [
      "Judgement: class feature fits a new runner verb. architectural would apply only if the verb becomes a new subsystem or breaks an interface, and the rules do not settle that (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/3/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C2). All three topic-3 seats assess the class as feature.",
      "Judgement: an advance verb that starts repair or review itself would contradict ADR 0021's hand-back, and one that only names the next step would match it (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/4/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C4, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/8/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C6). The repository does not decide whether the amendment binds a separate verb (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/3/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C7).",
      "Judgement: the loop's handoff refuses rather than infers state, so a verb that inferred a phase from findings.md alone would reconstruct state the runner deliberately refuses to reconstruct (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/8/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C6).",
      "Assumption: a verb that writes a change's status or header without taking the per-change record lock would become a second writer beside the runner's record (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/8/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C6).",
      "Judgement: the neighbour artefacts leave open who owns the runner's next-step line and in what order advance-verb, ladder-next-step, repair-hand-held-rows and verify-two-slots merge (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/5/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C7). No neighbour names advance-verb (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/5/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C7). repair-hand-held-rows relates only through the shared repair path (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/5/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C5). The packet's neighbour list is the only neighbour set in view (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/5/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C7).",
      "Judgement: the red-first test for advance must be written new. The only coverage it would inherit is the refusal sweep and inventory recognition, and its target entry point is still undetermined (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/7/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C7).",
      "Judgement from CLI guidance: an advance verb should follow the tool's existing verb grammar, appear in help, report the stage it left and the stage it entered, and keep its output short (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C2, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:qwen3.8-flash/C2, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:qwen3.8-flash/C3, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C3).",
      "Assumption and judgement: an implicit advance is safe only when the successor is a single stage. With branching or edited workflows, the verb should refuse or require an explicit target (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C6, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C5). Declarative transitions with a manual override are an alternative, held with low confidence (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C4).",
      "Judgement: the retrieved CLI guidance gives no workflow rules for legal transitions, branching, permissions or terminal states (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C4).",
      "Judgement: a stage-advancing verb fed by externally influenced state falls in the same failure class as CI triggers that act on untrusted input (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/11/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C5). This applies to work-item stages only by analogy (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/11/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C4).",
      "Judgement: Beads' Go module path still names steveyegge/beads after the repository moved to gastownhall (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/10/opencode-go:qwen3.8-flash/C3)."

      "Doctrine has repeatedly run ahead of its texts. The 72 + 6N swarm ceiling was decided on 2026-11-10 while the runner and WORKFLOW still stated 39 + 3N until 2026-11-12. Phase 2a was made mandatory on 2026-11-20 (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/6/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C7, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/6/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C5, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/6/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C6, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/6/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C4, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/6/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C5).",
      "Corrections in this history are recorded as dated notes or new commits, not rewrites (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/6/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C6). ADR 0020 point 3 bounds topic-6 history to ten commits per mapped path (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/6/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C7). Dropping CLAUDE.md left a recorded, still unresolved limit on Claude Code reading AGENTS.md directly (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/6/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C7).",
      "Test evidence for runner verbs comes only from stand-ins: World scripts the replies and tests assert on recorded calls. Red-first is registered through the plan's criterion ledger, which the gate checks as text. A STAGE2_PLANT_FAULT run does not count as verification (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/7/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C5, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/7/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C6). Harness CLI tests provide templates for exit 2 with no write and for single-record writes (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/7/claude-code-plan:claude-haiku-5-5/C4, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/7/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C6).",
      "The documented security boundary is fail-closed checks and prompts, not a sandbox. A leak check that cannot measure blocks with no fallback, Codex and Pi reads outside the worktree are bounded only by the prompt, and explore neutralises forged research-swarm/v2 markers before publishing (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/8/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C7). check_frontmatter_current.stamp leaves the text unchanged when there is no header or more than one updated: line (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/8/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C7).",
      "clig.dev names these as its CLI design concerns: human-first design, simple parts that work together, consistency across programs, saying just enough, ease of discovery, conversation as the norm, and robustness (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C1, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:qwen3.8-flash/C1, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C1, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C2).",
      "GitHub documents project stage movement as built-in automations, and GitLab documents inline quick actions on work items (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C3, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C5). GitHub publishes REST issue endpoints and a gh manual that includes gh issue close (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C1, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C2, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/10/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C1, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/10/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C1, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/10/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C2). XState publishes a concepts page on statecharts (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C3).",
      "Public tracker CLIs exist: ankitpokhrel/jira-cli, and Beads, a 'distributed graph issue tracker for AI agents, powered by Dolt', now at gastownhall/beads with a licence badge and a release badge. No retrieved page showed a dedicated advance or next-stage verb, its syntax, or a tool's version or licence (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/10/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C1, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/10/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C2, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/10/opencode-go:qwen3.8-flash/C1, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/10/opencode-go:qwen3.8-flash/C2, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/10/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C4, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/10/opencode-go:qwen3.8-flash/C4, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/10/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C3, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/10/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C6, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/10/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C4, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/9/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C7).",
      "Linear's GraphQL-mutations deep link redirects to a general developers landing page (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/10/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C2).",
      "GitHub Security Lab's guidance of 2021-08-03 warns that combining pull_request_target with a checkout of untrusted pull-request code enables cache poisoning and untrusted code execution (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/11/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C1, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/11/opencode-go:deepseek-v4.1-flash/C2).",
      "Advisory and CVE queries yielded no readable records. GitHub Advisory Database queries returned app shells, NVD redirected to its home page, and CVE.org required JavaScript. Jira's transition and workflow REST references were reachable but delivered as apps, and GitHub's issue docs showed no incident content (bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/11/opencode-go:qwen3.8-flash/C2, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/11/opencode-go:qwen3.8-flash/C3, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/11/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C1, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/11/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C2, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/11/opencode-go:hy4-flash-free/C3, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/11/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C1, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/11/opencode-go:qwen3.8-flash/C1, bf9a45e85a44e4a95f12a03ccafaf5a1/11/opencode-go:glm-5.3-flash/C2)."
